headline: High risk: Aider can write shared git state while cognee ingests sensitive support data, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuses.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, so malicious content in files can influence its prompts. Cognee handles documents and workflows, so if its outputs are copied into the repo or vice versa, the pair has a plausible instruction-injection bridge. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into git-tracked files that Aider reads
IF Aider is asked to edit files containing attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a review-only branch before applying edits
Add a manual prompt-scrubbing step for any cognee-generated text
Keep cognee outputs out of files Aider parses as instructions
Use separate repos or worktrees for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If Aider is pointed at the same workspace or receives cognee-derived documents, sensitive data can flow to third-party model providers by default. Cognee’s allowlisted egress does not remove the leakage path.
conditions: IF cognee data classes include personal data, finance data, or support history
IF Aider is given access to the same files or transcripts that contain those data classes
mitigations: Remove sensitive fields before Aider sees the files
Use a redaction pass on cognee outputs
Run Aider with a separate non-production workspace
Rotate and scope model-provider keys narrowly
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state is via a shared git repo. Cognee is a CLI agent with session memory and may also operate on shared documents or workflows. That overlapping mutable surface creates a real write-conflict risk in default multi-instance use, especially around git history and repo contents.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or shared document set
IF cognee writes back derived content while Aider commits changes
mitigations: Serialize writes with a single-owner workflow
Use separate branches per agent
Pause one agent while the other commits
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces git commits from edited files, and cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If cognee consumes Aider-produced artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into persisted repo changes or downstream workflow decisions. The pair does not show explicit autonomous action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF cognee treats Aider-edited files as authoritative inputs
IF Aider commits changes derived from unverified cognee outputs
mitigations: Add a human review gate before commits
Require source citations for any cognee-derived claim
Compare outputs against original documents
Limit Aider to draft-only changes
requires-engineering: add verification checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider can handle source code and git history with broad egress, while cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If those regulated data classes are processed together, residency or retention mismatches can create a compliance breach. Only Aider is cited for its egress and secrets handling because the compliance concern is driven by its outbound processing path; cognee supplies the regulated data classes.
conditions: IF personal data, finance data, or support history are processed through both agents
IF retention or residency rules differ between the Aider workspace and cognee deployment
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Aider inputs
Confirm a DPA and residency policy for cognee
Separate production support data from coding workspaces
Minimize logging of shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement retention controls across both systems
